records.does_not_establish: A recital states policy intent, not measured outcomes. It cuts both ways for home treatment: more tap-water drinking could expand point-of-use use, or greater confidence could reduce the felt need for it.

records.title: A Test of Conspicuous Consumption: Visibility and Income Elasticities (Review of Economics and Statistics)
records.excerpt: This paper shows that, consistent with a signaling-by-consuming model à la Veblen, income elasticities can be predicted from the visibility of consumer expenditures. We outline a stylized conspicuous consumption model where income elasticity is endogenously predicted to be higher if a good is visible and lower if it is not.

records.title: Status and the Demand for Visible Goods: Experimental Evidence on Conspicuous Consumption (Clingingsmith and Sheremeta, MPRA)
records.excerpt: We conduct an experiment in which we vary both whether a purchase of a physical product is publicly visible or kept private and whether the income used for purchase is linked to social status or randomly assigned. Making consumption choices visible leads to a large increase in demand when income is linked to status, but not otherwise.

records.title: Moondust and marketing magic · USPTO Journeys of Innovation

records.title: Moondust and marketing magic · USPTO Journeys of Innovation
records.excerpt: However, the researchers also uncovered a bright spot: 92% of women users were highly satisfied with the handheld Spot-Vac component of the Mod 4, which they often borrowed from their husbands' workshops to clean up small kitchen spills.
records.population: women users of an existing product (sample size not given)
records.does_not_establish: Satisfaction among people who already used a borrowed tool. It does not show that others would pay for a stand-alone vacuum, and the sample and question wording are not reported. Written after the decision date.

records.excerpt: First, that market research needed to be done before inventing a new product, not after. Second, consumers needed to be educated about new technology.

records.title: Moondust and marketing magic · USPTO Journeys of Innovation
records.excerpt: In contrast to almost all B&D products intended for men, [the new product] needed to be one aimed primarily at women, to be used upstairs in the home, not the basement," wrote Gantz.

records.title: Spinoff from a Moon Tool · NASA Spinoff

records.title: US4011624A - Cordless vacuum cleaner - Google Patents

records.title: US4011624A - Cordless vacuum cleaner - Google Patents

records.title: Black & Decker DustBuster · Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)
records.excerpt: The Mod 4 series was introduced in 1974 but was generally not successful in the marketplace.
records.does_not_establish: An encyclopedia summary, editable by anyone, that repeats the company story. Not independent of it. Written after the decision date.

records.excerpt: Vanek argued that time spent in housework had barely changed since 1926, despite the diffusion of practically every known domestic appliance over this period.

records.excerpt: The analysis of this data show that domestic technology rarely reduces women's unpaid working time and even, paradoxically, produces some increases in domestic labour.

records.title: Engines of Liberation · RePEc IDEAS (Review of Economic Studies abstract)
records.excerpt: It is argued here that the consumer goods revolution was conducive to liberating women from the home.
records.does_not_establish: A model-based argument about the whole century of appliances. It does not speak to any single product. Written after the decision date.

records.title: The sled that steers · USPTO Journeys of Innovation

records.excerpt: Demand for agricultural implements was unpredictable, with farmers tending to wait until they had sold a season's crop before ordering new tools and equipment. To fulfill these orders in a timely fashion, Allen's workers stayed busy in the fall, winter, and spring but had little to do in the summer months.
records.does_not_establish: Describes the idle-capacity problem. It shows a reason to want a summer product, not that sleds were the right one. Written after the decision date.

records.title: The sled that steers · USPTO Journeys of Innovation
records.excerpt: Some such summers, Allen's factory closed entirely and then had to rehire workers in a rush when the orders picked up again. Not everyone returned, however, and the cost of training new workers weighed on the company every fall.

records.title: The sled that steers · USPTO Journeys of Innovation

records.title: The sled that steers · USPTO Journeys of Innovation
records.excerpt: The component parts—wooden seat, steering lever, metal trusses—also constituted the Planet Jr. line of cultivators. The firm's workers already had the skills and machinery to make the Flexible Flyer even before Allen invented it.

records.title: The sled that steers · USPTO Journeys of Innovation

records.title: The sled that steers · USPTO Journeys of Innovation
records.excerpt: In the 1840s and '50s, American children (or the adults in their communities) tended to make sleds rather than buy them.
records.does_not_establish: Describes habits decades before the decision. Whether families still made their own sleds in the 1880s is not stated. Written after the decision date.

records.title: The sled that steers · USPTO Journeys of Innovation
records.excerpt: Of those sleds available for purchase, toboggans were the norm, despite the existence of a few sleds with runners. None came with a workable steering mechanism.

records.title: The sled that steers · USPTO Journeys of Innovation
records.excerpt: Allen was not the only adult to enjoy sledding. In this 1886 advertisement, Star Toboggans of Chicago appealed directly to grownups in search of winter fun.

records.title: The sled that steers · USPTO Journeys of Innovation

records.excerpt: One of them, a periodical called "Farm and Garden," reached a circulation of 50,000.
records.does_not_establish: Shows the firm could reach farmers in print. Farmers are not the same audience as toy and hardware buyers. Written after the decision date.

records.title: The sled that steers · USPTO Journeys of Innovation
records.excerpt: The children at Westtown knew a good thing when they saw it, to be sure, but not the big buyers like hardware and department stores. To these retailers, the Flexible Flyer looked too different from the familiar sleds and toboggans of their youth.
records.does_not_establish: Describes how retailers reacted after the decision date, so it was not knowable then. It is the trade buyer's view, not the end user's. Written after the decision date.

records.title: US381665A - Sled - Google Patents
records.excerpt: relates particularly to that class of sleds known as double runners, in which the seat or platform is supported upon two bobs or single sleds; and it consists of the devices and improvements hereinafter described.

records.excerpt: consists of an improved sled embodying certain novel features of construction, the details of which are hereinafter fully described, and wherein the steering is accomplished by the lateral bending of the runners.
records.does_not_establish: Granted after the decision date. A patent shows what was claimed, not that buyers valued steering.

records.title: Hours of Work in U.S. History · EH.net Encyclopedia
records.excerpt: Atack and Bateman (1992), using data from census manuscripts, estimate average weekly hours to be 60.1 in 1880 — very close to Weeks' contemporary estimate.
records.does_not_establish: An average for manufacturing workers. It shows how little free time adults had, not how much children sledded or what families spent on toys.

records.title: Hours of Work in U.S. History · EH.net Encyclopedia
records.excerpt: In 1880 a typical male household head had very little leisure time — only about 1.8 hours per day over the course of a year.
records.does_not_establish: A historical estimate about adults, not children, and it does not measure spending on leisure goods.

records.title: Child Labor in the United States · EH.net Encyclopedia

records.does_not_establish: Shows many older children worked in 1880, which limits the time for play. It says nothing about younger children or about families' toy budgets.

records.title: Flexible Flyer · Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)
records.excerpt: Allen began producing sleds in his farm equipment factory to keep his workers busy during the slow season.
records.does_not_establish: An encyclopedia summary, editable by anyone, that repeats the company story. Not independent of it. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Infrared Thermometer · NASA Spinoff

records.excerpt: Diatek Corporation, San Diego, CA and the Jet Propulsion Lab developed the Diatek Model 7000 aural thermometer which weighs only eight ounces, and measures temperature in less than two seconds using infrared astronomy technology to measure the amount of infrared energy emitted by the eardrum (the same way temperature of stars and planets is measured).
records.does_not_establish: An agency summary of performance figures supplied by the maker. NASA states that it does not confirm such claims, and speed in a ward is not demand in a home.

records.title: Infrared Thermometer · NASA Spinoff
records.date: 1991 (originally published; note on later acquisition added afterwards)
records.excerpt: This method avoids contact with mucous membranes, virtually eliminating the possibility of cross infection, and permits temperature measurement of newborn, critically ill, or incapacitated patients.

records.title: Infrared Thermometer · NASA Spinoff
records.date: 1991 (originally published; note on later acquisition added afterwards)
records.excerpt: Diatek Corporation was purchased by Welch Allyn Inc. The Diatek Model 7000 is now marketed as SureTemp.

records.title: Slice of History: Infrared Ear Thermometer · NASA JPL
records.excerpt: In 1991, Diatek Corporation of San Diego put a new infrared thermometer - Model 7000 - on the market. Early electronic thermometers had been used by some hospitals and doctors' offices for several years before that time, but this Diatek model was a pioneering effort to modify space-based infrared sensors for a medical infrared thermometer.
records.does_not_establish: An archivist's note on the professional launch. It does not cover home thermometers. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Slice of History: Infrared Ear Thermometer · NASA JPL

records.title: US4797840A - Infrared electronic thermometer and method for measuring temperature - Google Patents
records.excerpt: A further object of the invention is to provide a noncontacting electronic thermometer for medical use which is compact, inexpensive and convenient and easy to use.

records.title: Effect of otitis media on infrared tympanic thermometry · Clin Pediatr 1991 (PubMed abstract)

records.excerpt: This difference is of minimal clinical significance and does not affect the accuracy when compared to oral or rectal control readings.

records.title: Fever phobia: misconceptions of parents about fevers · Am J Dis Child 1980 (PubMed abstract)

records.title: Fever phobia: misconceptions of parents about fevers · Am J Dis Child 1980 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: The great concern of parents about fever is not justified. Health education to counteract "fever phobia" should be a part of routine pediatric care.
records.population: 81 parents at a hospital-based pediatric clinic
records.does_not_establish: A recommendation that doctors reduce parental worry, which could cut against a product sold on frequent checking. It is an opinion, not a measured effect.

records.title: The ability of mothers to read a thermometer · Clin Pediatr 1990 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: Ninety-three percent of suburban practice parents could read three pre-set thermometers correctly, but only 10% of urban practice parents could perform the same task.
records.population: 200 mothers in one suburban and one urban practice
records.does_not_establish: Shows that some parents struggle with glass thermometers, so a digital reading may help them. Two practices are not a national sample, and nothing here is about willingness to pay.

records.title: Reading a thermometer by use of temperature zones · Am J Dis Child 1990 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: Although 57.9% of parents owned a mercury glass thermometer, only 9.7% could accurately read three thermometers presented to them.

records.does_not_establish: A single urban clinic. The same study found a cheap teaching fix, so the problem may not need a new device.

records.title: Reliability of infrared tympanic thermometry in the detection of rectal fever in children · Ann Emerg Med 1995 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: The poor sensitivity of ITT in detecting fever and high fever may result in clinically important miscategorizations of individual patients.
records.does_not_establish: A study of professional use in an emergency department. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Infrared ear thermometry compared with rectal thermometry in children: a systematic review · Lancet 2002 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: Our finding suggests that infrared ear thermometry does not show sufficient agreement with an established method of temperature measurement to be used in situations where body temperature needs to be measured with precision.
records.does_not_establish: A systematic review of clinical accuracy. Parents may accept less precision for speed, so this does not settle home demand. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Infrared ear thermometry compared with rectal thermometry in children: a systematic review · Lancet 2002 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: Infrared ear thermometry is frequently used in children, because this is a quick method of taking temperature and the ear is easily accessible.

records.title: Airing Out Anthrax · NASA Spinoff 2002
records.excerpt: It is essentially a spinoff of the company's Bio-KES system, a highly effective device used by the produce industry for ethylene gas removal to aid in preserving the freshness of fruits, vegetables, and flowers.

records.excerpt: The available unit, which is a flat, metal box approximately the size of a tabletop, is designed to be mounted to a ceiling, but can be placed on a wall, if necessary.

records.title: Airing Out Anthrax · NASA Spinoff 2002
records.excerpt: In addition, KES in planning to develop a residential model of the AiroCide TiO2, in response to an overwhelming demand from homeowners looking to stave off common household allergens.

records.title: Air Purifiers Eliminate Pathogens, Preserve Food · NASA Spinoff 2009

records.excerpt: Reeves Floral, an AiroCide user, reported 92-percent reductions in airborne mold and a 58-percent drop in airborne bacteria levels in just the first 24 hours it had the units operating in its floral storage warehouse.

records.title: Home Air Purifiers Eradicate Harmful Pathogens · NASA Spinoff 2013
records.excerpt: Previously designed for industrial spaces, there is now a specially designed unit for home use.

records.title: Home Air Purifiers Eradicate Harmful Pathogens · NASA Spinoff 2013
records.excerpt: According to testimonials shared on the Airocide website, people credit the product with helping them and their loved ones attain relief from symptoms associated with asthma, allergies, and sinuses.

records.does_not_establish: An agency complaint seeking a penalty, not a finding after trial. It shows where the regulator draws the line on claims, not how the case ended or whether buyers cared.

records.title: EPA issues complaint for illegal claims that pesticide product protects children from bacterial infections · US EPA news release
records.excerpt: The use of unapproved public health claims in conjunction with the sale of consumer goods such as sponges, toys and cutting boards may pose a risk to the public.
records.does_not_establish: Names the kinds of household goods carrying the additive in 1997. It does not give volumes, which partners made them, or whether they sold well.

records.title: EPA acts to prevent Playskool toy manufacturer Hasbro, Inc., from false claims about protecting children from microbial infections · US EPA news release

records.does_not_establish: Shows that a large toy maker put the additive into products for children in 1997. It does not show sales of those toys or whether the tie-up continued.

records.title: EPA acts to prevent Playskool toy manufacturer Hasbro, Inc., from false claims about protecting children from microbial infections · US EPA news release

records.does_not_establish: The cost fell on the partner brand, not on the additive supplier. It does not show the cost of compliance in 2016 or how the corrections affected sales.

records.title: Toy company fined for antibacterial claims · The Spokesman-Review (Associated Press)

records.does_not_establish: Shows the gap between the claim a consumer brand wanted and the claim it was allowed. It does not show whether the permitted wording still persuades buyers.

records.title: 40 CFR 152.25 Exemptions for pesticides of a character not requiring FIFRA regulation · Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School

records.does_not_establish: The exemption text as published now; it has been in force since before the decision date, but this page does not show its 2016 wording. It says nothing about demand.

records.title: PRN 2000-1: Applicability of the Treated Articles Exemption to Antimicrobial Pesticides · US EPA

records.does_not_establish: A law firm summary of enforcement against retailers and makers, not specifically against Microban or its partners. It shows the risk retailers carry, not how often cases arose in 2016.

records.title: Consumer antibacterial soaps: effective or just risky? · Clinical Infectious Diseases (PubMed abstract)

records.title: Revolution in photography: the first 35mm camera · University of Wuppertal
records.excerpt: The Imperial Patent Office, where the original Leica was to be registered, noted that it infringed a patent held by Carl Zeiss/Jena and a French patent. Consequently, only the ‘little brother’ of the patent – utility model protection – was initially granted.
records.does_not_establish: A university interview with an art historian. It shows weak legal protection against rivals such as Zeiss, not whether rivals would copy the design. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Loban on Leica, 1913 to 1935: innovations and impacts · Photographic Historical Society of Canada
records.excerpt: When the post war recession left the company with excess capacity, a short run of cameras, called the “Null Series” was produced and handed out to selected photographers for trial use.
records.does_not_establish: A society talk summary based on published histories. It ties the pilot run to spare capacity, which is a supply reason, not proof of demand. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Oskar Barnack · Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)
records.excerpt: In 1923 Barnack convinced his boss, Ernst Leitz II , to make a series of 31 pre-production cameras for the factory and for outdoor photographers. Although the prototypes received a mixed reception, Ernst Leitz decided in 1924 to produce the camera.
records.population: factory staff and outside photographers given 31 pre-production cameras
records.does_not_establish: An encyclopedia summary, editable by anyone, drawing partly on company histories. The number of cameras differs between sources (25 or 31), and "mixed reception" is not a measured result. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Loban on Leica, 1913 to 1935: innovations and impacts · Photographic Historical Society of Canada
records.excerpt: Feedback from the photographers was unfavourable, but regardless, Ernst Leitz decided to manufacture Barnack’s camera.
records.population: selected photographers in the pilot run
records.does_not_establish: A second-hand summary of the pilot feedback; no numbers or reasons are given. It counts against demand but does not say whether the faults were fixable. Written after the decision date.

records.title: The History of the Leica I · Leica Camera AG
records.excerpt: Leitz developed this small series of prototypes in order to test them under real-life conditions. Cameras were distributed to photographers, employees and experts so that they could gain practical experience with them.
records.does_not_establish: The company's own centenary account. It describes the pilot run but reports no results from it. Written after the decision date.

records.title: The History of the Leica I · Leica Camera AG
records.excerpt: Nobody could foresee whether a full-frame 35 mm format camera would be well-received. The market was uncertain and production costs high. The company’s reputation was at stake.
records.does_not_establish: The company's own retrospective view of the risks. It gives no figures for costs or the expected market. Written after the decision date.

records.title: The History of the Leica I · Leica Camera AG
records.excerpt: There was internal resistance and many managers and engineers were sceptical of series production in 1924.
records.does_not_establish: The company's own account, written to celebrate a bold decision. It does not say what the sceptics' reasons were. Written after the decision date.

records.title: 100 years of Leica: how a 'miniature format' took over the world of cameras forever · Digital Camera World
records.excerpt: He really wanted to build Barnack’s camera, but not all his senior managers agreed with the idea because it would cost a lot to tool up for production and the unproven ‘miniature format’ (i.e. 35mm) was considered too much of a risk.
records.does_not_establish: A magazine retelling drawn largely from company sources. It names tooling cost and an unproven format as the objections, without amounts. Written after the decision date.

records.title: 100 years of Leica: how a 'miniature format' took over the world of cameras forever · Digital Camera World
records.excerpt: Explaining his decision, he stated, “This small camera is an opportunity to create work for our employees – if it lives up to the promise I see in it – through the years of the Depression and to get them through the difficult times ahead.”
records.does_not_establish: The owner's stated motive, quoted long after. Keeping workers busy is a reason to produce, not evidence that buyers want the product. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Ernst Leitz II · Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)
records.excerpt: German hyperinflation and the lack of interest on the part of the photographic trade in converting to the new technology hampered the market launch.
records.does_not_establish: An encyclopedia summary, editable by anyone, drawing partly on company histories. Points to a dealer channel the firm did not control and that was reluctant. It does not measure how many dealers refused. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic · Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)
records.excerpt: By 1924 the currency had stabilised and German reparations payments began again under the Dawes Plan
records.does_not_establish: An encyclopedia summary, editable by anyone, drawing partly on company histories. Gives the general economic setting in the decision year. It says nothing about spending on cameras. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Leica Camera · Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)
records.excerpt: By 1925, around 900 cameras had been sold, and more than 1,600 in the following year. From 1927 onwards, the camera business was profitable and sold more than 3,200 cameras.
records.does_not_establish: An encyclopedia summary, editable by anyone, drawing partly on company histories. Reveals the outcome after the decision, so it must not be used to judge what was knowable in 1924. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Company history (沿革) · Tanita Corporation
records.excerpt: 1959年 (昭和34年) ・はかり製造許可証取得 ・ヘルスメーター製造開始
records.does_not_establish: The company's own timeline, in Japanese: in 1959 it obtained a scale-manufacturing licence and began making 'health meters' (personal weighing scales). It does not say who bought them or under whose brand. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Company history (沿革) · Tanita Corporation
records.excerpt: 1979年 (昭和54年) ・ヘルスメーター1000万台達成
records.does_not_establish: The company's own timeline: 10 million health meters reached by 1979. A cumulative production count, not annual sales, market share or brand recognition. Written after the decision date.

records.title: タニタ (Tanita) · Japanese Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)
records.excerpt: 日本で初めて家庭用 体重計 を製造・販売。「ヘルスメーター」と命名した。
records.does_not_establish: An encyclopedia summary in Japanese: the firm made and sold Japan's first household weighing scale and named it 'health meter'. It repeats the company's own claim to be first. Written after the decision date.

records.title: タニタ (Tanita) · Japanese Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)
records.excerpt: 独自の技術力で様々な製品を製造するが、かつては OEM による受託生産が主で、自社ブランド製品は少なかったという
records.does_not_establish: An encyclopedia summary in Japanese: the firm once made mostly OEM products for others and had few own-brand products. It is hearsay ("it is said") and gives no dates or shares, so how strong its own brand was before 1994 stays open. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Tanita supports "TIGER & BUNNY 2" · Tanita Corporation
records.excerpt: Tanita is a world leader in precision electronic scales. With almost 50% of its domestic market share, the name Tanita is a household name in Japan.
records.does_not_establish: A recent promotional page. The share figure is the company's own, undated and unsourced, and describes the present, not 1993. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Tanita Corp. of America company profile · DAIC (Diagnostic and Interventional Cardiology)
records.excerpt: Based on medical evidence linking excess body fat to heart disease, diabetes and certain cancers, Tanita introduced the world’s first integrated body composition analyzer/scale to the professional markets in 1992.
records.does_not_establish: A company-supplied profile on a trade directory. It states the professional launch and its health rationale; it does not show home buyers want body-fat numbers. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Promoting Health through "Measuring Devices" · Hiragana Times
records.excerpt: In Japan, every household has a bathroom scale (health meter), and most nowadays keep track of your body composition.
records.does_not_establish: A magazine feature about the company, written two decades later. "Every household" is a loose claim, not a survey figure. Written after the decision date.

records.title: US5415176A, Apparatus for measuring body fat · Google Patents
records.excerpt: A body fat measuring apparatus for measuring body fat in a patient's body comprises apparatus for simultaneously measuring an impedance between the patient's feet, and for measuring the patient's height and the patient's weight
records.does_not_establish: A patent records what the applicant claimed. It frames the user as a patient and does not show the device works well enough for unsupervised use. Granted after the decision date. Written after the decision date.

records.title: US5415176A, Apparatus for measuring body fat · Google Patents
records.excerpt: the impedance value of a body to be measured vary according to the date, time and differences of body condition before measurement. These various are too large to use the above-described inference formula accurately and amount of body fat calculated by the formula is likely to be inaccurate.
records.does_not_establish: The applicant's own account of why readings vary with the time of day and body condition. It shows the firm knew of the accuracy problem; it does not show whether its design solved it in homes. Granted after the decision date. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Assessment of fat-free mass using bioelectrical impedance measurements of the human body · Am J Clin Nutr 1985 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: This method is safe, noninvasive, provides rapid measurements, requires little operator skill and subject cooperation, and is portable. Further validation of this method is recommended in subjects with abnormal body composition.
records.does_not_establish: A small laboratory study with a four-electrode research instrument, not a foot-pad scale. Ease of use for operators is not the same as accuracy at home.

records.title: Body composition assessment of athletes using bioelectrical impedance measurements · J Sports Med Phys Fitness 1990 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: These findings indicate the need for controlled measurement conditions to obtain valid body composition estimates using the TBI method in healthy people.
records.does_not_establish: Uses a tetrapolar method, not foot-to-foot, in athletes. It suggests uncontrolled home readings may be off, but does not test a home device.

records.title: Bioelectrical impedance analysis in body composition measurement: NIH Technology Assessment Conference Statement · Am J Clin Nutr 1996 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: BIA values are affected by numerous variables including body position, hydration status, consumption of food and beverages, ambient air and skin temperature, recent physical activity, and conductance of the examining table.
records.population: expert panel review of the literature
records.does_not_establish: An expert panel on BIA in general, aimed at physicians. It does not assess a home scale or what buyers would accept. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Bioimpedance analysis: evaluation of leg-to-leg system based on pressure contact footpad electrodes · Med Sci Sports Exerc 1997 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: Conventional single frequency bioimpedance analysis (BIA) systems require technician placement of arm and leg gel electrodes, a suitable location for recumbent measurements, and a separate measurement of body weight.
records.population: healthy adults in a hospital research unit
records.does_not_establish: Describes why the older clinical method was hard to use outside a clinic. It does not show that ease of use creates demand. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Evaluation of the novel Tanita body-fat analyser to measure body composition by comparison with a four-compartment model · Br J Nutr 2000 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: In 104 men and 101 women (16-78 years and BMI 16-41 kg/m2) the mean bias in body-fat mass measured using the Tanita body-fat analyser was 0.8 (2SD 7.9) kg relative to a four-compartment model.
records.does_not_establish: Small average bias but wide limits for individuals, measured with a professional model under laboratory conditions. It says nothing about buyer demand. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Validity of foot-to-foot bio-electrical impedance analysis body composition estimates in overweight and obese children · Int J Body Compos Res 2009 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: The Tanita TBF-310 foot-to-foot BIA body composition analyser with the manufacturer's prediction equations is not recommended for application to individual children who are overweight and obese
records.does_not_establish: A small study in one group with a professional model. It counts against individual accuracy but not against use for tracking trends. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Bioelectrical impedance analysis · Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)
records.excerpt: BIA is not considered sufficiently accurate for recording of single measurements of individuals, but it can be acceptable for measuring groups and also for tracking body composition in an individual over a period of time.
records.does_not_establish: An encyclopedia summary of later research. It suggests a home use (tracking over time) the method suits, but does not show buyers want it. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Twenty-year changes in the prevalence of overweight in Japanese adults: the National Nutrition Survey 1976-95 · Obes Rev 2002 (PubMed abstract)
records.excerpt: The prevalence of preobese (BMI: 25-29.9kg m(-2)) and obese (BMI > or = 30 kg m(-2)) men increased from 14.5% and 0.8%, respectively, in the time-period 1976-80 to 20.5% and 2.01% during 1991-95.
records.population: national survey sample of 91983 men and 120822 women
records.does_not_establish: Shows rising overweight among Japanese men; the same paper reports no change for women overall. Concern about weight is not proof of willingness to pay for a body-fat reading. Published after the decision date, though most data predate it. Written after the decision date.

records.title: 21 CFR 870.2770 Impedance plethysmograph · eCFR (US Government Publishing Office)
records.excerpt: The device, when it is a body composition analyzer which is not intended to diagnose or treat any medical condition, is exempt from the premarket notification procedures in subpart E of part 807 of this chapter
records.does_not_establish: US rules in their current form, not Japanese rules in 1993. It shows a body composition analyser without diagnostic claims faces light review in the US today. Written after the decision date.

records.title: FDA Approves First Oral Fluid Based Rapid HIV Test Kit (FDA news release, reprinted) · NATAP
records.excerpt: The original version of this rapid test -- the OraQuick Rapid HIV-1/2 Antibody Test, manufactured by OraSure Technologies, Inc., Bethlehem , Pa. -- was approved November 7, 2002 for detection of antibody to HIV-1 in blood.
records.does_not_establish: Approval for use by trained staff. It says nothing about whether untrained people can run or read the test.

records.title: FDA Approves First Oral Fluid Based Rapid HIV Test Kit (FDA news release, reprinted) · NATAP
records.excerpt: The OraQuick Rapid HIV-1/2 Antibody test for use on blood was categorized as a waived test under CLIA (Clinical Laboratory Improvements Amendments of 1988) in January, 2003. A waived test system can be given in facilities with any CLIA certificate, rather than only in facilities certified for higher complexity tests.
records.does_not_establish: A waiver widens use to more health-care settings, which is still not sale to the public.

records.title: FDA Approves First Oral Fluid Based Rapid HIV Test Kit (FDA news release, reprinted) · NATAP
records.excerpt: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has estimated that one fourth of the approximately 900,000 HIV-infected people in the U.S. are not aware that they are infected.
records.does_not_establish: Sizes the unmet need for testing, not the number who would buy and use a test on their own.

records.title: 510(k) Premarket Notification K023487 · US FDA
records.excerpt: Device Name HISTOFREEZER WART REMOVAL SYSTEM OR OTHER PROPRIETARY NAME Applicant OraSure Technologies, Inc.
records.does_not_establish: A regulatory database entry. It shows a clearance was granted, not how the product sells or through whom.

records.title: 510(k) Summary, Histofreezer Wart Removal System (K023487) · US FDA
records.excerpt: The Histofreezer@Wart Removal System is indicated for over-the-counter treatment of common warts and plantar warts.
records.population: people with common or plantar warts
records.does_not_establish: The company's own submission. Wart removal is low risk and far from an infectious-disease diagnosis, so the precedent may not carry over.

records.title: 510(k) Summary, Histofreezer Wart Removal System (K023487) · US FDA
records.excerpt: Histofreezer@ labeling has also been developed to provide adequate information for the consumer to make a self diagnosis and to ensure that they contact their doctor if in any doubt, if stinging or aching persists after treatment, or if the wart does not improve after four treatments.
records.does_not_establish: Shows experience writing self-use labelling for a simple device, not that lay users would follow instructions for an HIV test.

records.title: FDA to Consider Rapid, At-Home HIV Test (HealthDay, reprinted) · NATAP
records.excerpt: The tests, which have become extremely popular in just a year, are now available at doctors' offices for $12 to $17 each.
records.does_not_establish: The professional price per test, not what individuals would pay for a self-test with counselling support.

records.title: FDA to Consider Rapid, At-Home HIV Test (HealthDay, reprinted) · NATAP
records.excerpt: Currently, people can take HIV tests at home, but they must send a blood sample to a laboratory and wait three to seven days for results, Spair said.
records.does_not_establish: The company's description of the existing alternative. It does not show that the wait is what keeps people from testing.

records.title: FDA considers allowing test for AIDS over the counter (Associated Press) · The Vindicator
records.excerpt: If approved, the test would become the first FDA-approved test that a person can take without the presence of a health care worker, or the requirement of mailing a sample to a lab.
records.does_not_establish: Describes what approval would mean. It does not predict whether or when the regulator would approve.

records.title: Approval sought in the U.S. for 20 minute home HIV test · News-Medical
records.excerpt: Although some HIV charities welcome wider use of home testing, many have expressed fears that people who find out in this way may kill themselves. They believe testing should be supervised and counselling provided on a face to face basis.
records.does_not_establish: Reports advocates' fears, not measured harm among people who tested themselves.

records.title: Approval sought in the U.S. for 20 minute home HIV test · News-Medical
records.excerpt: In the UK home HIV testing kits are banned for such reasons, but unapproved kits are available over the internet, and experts advise caution in this respect.
records.does_not_establish: Shows a major market closed by law in 2005. It does not show the US regulator would take the same view.

records.title: Home sample collection tests for HIV infection (JAMA) · PubMed
records.excerpt: During the first year of availability, 174316 HIV HSC tests were submitted to the manufacturers for analysis; 0.9% of the results were positive for HIV, and 97% of all users called to learn test results.
records.population: users of home sample collection kits, 1996-1997
records.does_not_establish: Demand for a mail-in kit with telephone counselling, which is a different product from an instant self-read test, and first-year use may not persist.

records.title: Anonymous HIV testing using home collection and telemedicine counseling (Arch Intern Med) · PubMed
records.excerpt: Subject-collected blood spot sample results were in complete agreement with venous blood sample results, demonstrating 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity compared with venous controls.
records.does_not_establish: Here a laboratory ran the test, so it shows lay people can collect a sample, not that they can perform and read a rapid test.

records.title: Overcoming barriers to HIV testing: preferences for new strategies (J Acquir Immune Defic Syndr) · PubMed
records.excerpt: The largest proportions of participants preferred rapid testing strategies, including clinic-based testing (27%) and home self-testing (20%); roughly equal proportions preferred oral fluid testing (18%), urine testing (17%), and standard blood testing (17%). One percent preferred home specimen collection.
records.population: 460 people at a needle exchange, sex venues and an STD clinic
records.does_not_establish: Stated preferences of high-risk people in one city, not willingness to pay or actual use.

records.title: Revised recommendations for HIV testing of adults, adolescents, and pregnant women in health-care settings (MMWR Recomm Rep) · PubMed
records.excerpt: For patients in all health-care settings HIV screening is recommended for patients in all health-care settings after the patient is notified that testing will be performed unless the patient declines (opt-out screening).
records.does_not_establish: Expands testing through clinics, the company's existing route, so it may reduce the need for self-testing. It does not address self-tests. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Rapid HIV testing at home: does it solve a problem or create one? (Ann Intern Med) · PubMed
records.excerpt: Home HIV testing will attract a predominantly affluent clientele, composed disproportionately of HIV-uninfected new couples and "worried well" persons, as well as very recently infected persons with undetectable disease.
records.does_not_establish: A modelling commentary, not observed buyer data. It argues the buyers would differ from those the public-health case relies on. Written after the decision date.

records.title: User acceptability and feasibility of self-testing with HIV rapid tests (J Acquir Immune Defic Syndr) · PubMed
records.excerpt: Nevertheless, 85% failed to perform all steps correctly, especially blood sampling, and 56% had invalid results because of incorrect test performance.
records.population: 350 people at two HIV testing centres
records.does_not_establish: Uses a blood-based rival test, not an oral swab, so the error rate may be lower with oral fluid. Written after the decision date.

records.title: HIV Home Testing · Clinical Laboratory News (AACC/ADLM)
records.excerpt: FDA rejected requests for OTC HIV tests as early as 1989. In 1996, the agency approved two home-use blood specimen collection kits, but these required the user to mail a self-collected specimen for lab testing and wait for results over the phone or in the mail.
records.does_not_establish: A history of regulatory positions. It does not say what evidence would satisfy the regulator in 2005. Written after the decision date.

records.title: HIV Home Testing · Clinical Laboratory News (AACC/ADLM)
records.excerpt: However, sensitivity dropped in comparison to professional use of the kit to 92.98% (95% CI: 86.64–96.92%)—notably with 86.64% for the lower bound of the 95% CI.
records.does_not_establish: Reveals the later trial result, which was not known in 2005. It reports accuracy, not demand. Written after the decision date.

records.title: FDA approves first rapid, at-home HIV test · NBC News
records.excerpt: OraSure expects the at-home HIV test to be available starting in October at more than 30,000 retail outlets across the U.S. and online, according to a company press release.
records.does_not_establish: A launch plan reported from a press release. It shows the later route, not sales or repeat purchase. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Health and Medicine · NASA Spinoff 2005
records.excerpt: When NASA determined that red LEDs could grow plants in space, Marshall Space Flight Center awarded QDI several Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) contracts to investigate the effectiveness of the broad-spectrum diodes in medical applications.
records.does_not_establish: Shows that government research contracts, not paying customers, funded the medical work. It does not show the medical benefit is proven. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Health and Medicine · NASA Spinoff 2005
records.excerpt: The WARP 10 (Warfighter Accelerated Recovery by Photobiomodulation) is a high-intensity, hand-held, portable LED unit intended for the temporary relief of minor muscle and joint pain, arthritis, stiffness, and muscle spasms.
records.does_not_establish: The maker's description of intended use, not evidence that the device relieves pain better than a placebo or a heat pad. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Health and Medicine · NASA Spinoff 2005
records.excerpt: The WARP 10 was designed to aid armed forces personnel on the front lines with immediate first aid care for minor injuries and pain, thereby improving endurance in combat.
records.does_not_establish: A design goal for soldiers. Soldiers issued a device do not pay for it, so this is no sign of willingness to pay among individuals. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Health and Medicine · NASA Spinoff 2005
records.excerpt: The U.S. Department of Defense and the U.S. Navy are currently issuing WARP 10 to crews on submarines and Special Forces operations.
records.does_not_establish: Institutional procurement as reported by the company through NASA. It gives no number of units and no outcome data. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Health and Medicine · NASA Spinoff 2005
records.excerpt: QDI has introduced an FDA-approved consumer version sharing the same power and properties of the military model, as an alternative to the cost and complications associated with overuse of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for persistent pain relief.
records.does_not_establish: Reveals a later launch and its positioning, not its sales or user satisfaction. "FDA-approved" overstates a 510(k) clearance. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Health and Medicine · NASA Spinoff 2005
records.excerpt: Furthermore, conservative calculations for the United States estimate that approximately 107,000 patients are hospitalized each year for NSAID-related gastrointestinal complications and at least 16,500 NSAID-related deaths occur annually among arthritis patients alone, according to compiled research.
records.does_not_establish: Second-hand figures on the harm of the main alternative. Harm from pills does not show that people would switch to a light device or that it works. Written after the decision date.

records.title: NASA Research Illuminates Medical Uses of Light · NASA Spinoff
records.excerpt: Two years after Ignatius’ death in 2011, Quantum Devices left the field of medical LEDs, and NASA didn’t end up using the technology in space.
records.does_not_establish: Reveals the later exit, without saying whether the medical line was profitable or why it ended. Written after the decision date.

records.title: NASA Research Illuminates Medical Uses of Light · NASA Spinoff
records.excerpt: The company’s business is now evenly split between home devices and the stationary units still used by physicians, athletic trainers, physical therapists, and chiropractors.
records.does_not_establish: Describes a different, later company (Multi Radiance Medical), so it shows a home market can exist, not that this firm could have reached it in 2003. Written after the decision date.

records.title: FAQ · NASA Spinoff
records.excerpt: While many commercial products are derived from NASA technology, NASA does not endorse these products; nor does NASA confirm manufacturers’ performance claims related to any particular spinoff development.
records.does_not_establish: The publisher's own warning that spinoff stories relay the makers' claims. It does not judge this device.

records.title: 510(k) Premarket Notification K032229 · US FDA
records.excerpt: Device Classification Name Lamp, Infrared, Therapeutic Heating 510(k) Number K032229 Device Name QUANTUM WARP 10 LIGHT DELIVERY SYSTEM
records.does_not_establish: Shows the clearance went through the therapeutic heating lamp category, which is a finding of substantial equivalence, not proof of clinical benefit. The clearance came after the decision date. Written after the decision date.

records.title: 21 CFR § 890.5500 - Infrared lamp · Cornell Legal Information Institute
records.excerpt: An infrared lamp is a device intended for medical purposes that emits energy at infrared frequencies (approximately 700 nanometers to 50,000 nanometers) to provide topical heating.
records.does_not_establish: The category is defined by topical heating, which limits what such a device can claim. The page shows the current text, including a 2019 amendment to the exemption rule.

records.title: Effect of NASA light-emitting diode irradiation on wound healing (J Clin Laser Med Surg) · PubMed
records.excerpt: LED produced improvement of greater than 40% in musculoskeletal training injuries in Navy SEAL team members, and decreased wound healing time in crew members aboard a U.S. Naval submarine.
records.does_not_establish: A review of the group's own data, co-authored by the company's founder (R Ignatius) and funded through NASA contracts. It is not an independent, blinded trial of pain relief.

records.title: NASA light-emitting diodes for the prevention of oral mucositis in pediatric bone marrow transplant patients (J Clin Laser Med Surg) · PubMed
records.excerpt: There were no significant differences between sides in OMI or pain. Conclusion: Although more studies are needed, LED therapy appears useful in the prevention of OM in pediatric BMT patients.
records.does_not_establish: A small study against historical controls in a hospital setting, with no difference between the treated and sham sides. It does not bear on muscle or joint pain in adults.

records.title: The effect of low-level laser therapy on musculoskeletal pain: a meta-analysis (Pain) · PubMed
records.excerpt: In the double-blind trials, the mean difference in pain between LLLT and placebo was 0.3% (S.E.(d) 4.6%, confidence limits -10.3-10.9%).
records.does_not_establish: Covers lasers, not LED arrays, and predates the newer dose-based reviews. The authors conclude there is no effect on pain.

records.title: The efficacy of laser therapy for musculoskeletal and skin disorders: a criteria-based meta-analysis (Phys Ther) · PubMed
records.excerpt: In general, the methodological quality of these studies appeared to be rather low.
records.does_not_establish: A judgement on trial quality for lasers. The same review finds an average effect larger than placebo for musculoskeletal disorders, so it cuts both ways.

records.title: Low level laser therapy (classes I, II and III) for the treatment of osteoarthritis (Cochrane Database Syst Rev) · PubMed
records.excerpt: For OA, the results are conflicting in different studies and may depend on the method of application and other features of the LLLT application.
records.does_not_establish: Five small laser trials; says nothing directly about LED devices or about use without a clinician.

records.title: A systematic review of low level laser therapy with location-specific doses for pain from chronic joint disorders (Aust J Physiother) · PubMed
records.excerpt: Low level laser therapy with the suggested dose range significantly reduces pain and improves health status in chronic joint disorders, but the heterogeneity in patient samples, treatment procedures and trial design calls for cautious interpretation of the results.
records.does_not_establish: Supportive, but for lasers applied by clinicians at set doses, not for an LED unit used by the person in pain. Published in 2003, possibly after the decision date. Published in mid-2003, after the decision date. Written after the decision date.

records.title: Trends in alternative medicine use in the United States, 1990-1997 (JAMA) · PubMed
records.excerpt: Use of at least 1 of 16 alternative therapies during the previous year increased from 33.8% in 1990 to 42.1% in 1997 (P < or = .001).
records.does_not_establish: Shows wide willingness to try non-drug therapies, often paid out of pocket, not demand for a light device in particular.

records.title: FTC Internet Health Fraud Law Enforcement and Consumer Education Campaign · US Federal Trade Commission
records.excerpt: "Operation Cure.All," targets companies touting bogus cancer cures and making unsubstantiated health claims, such as "magnetic therapy devices" can alleviate arthritis and high blood pressure.
